To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we have developed a novel differential approach to the measurement of transport coefficients in molecular junctions based on CT-AFM; (b) we have measured the transport coefficients of alkanethioles as a function of the length of the molecules, and (c) we have found that the tunneling decay constants of alkanethios are in good agreement with those obtained from other experimental and theoretical approaches.

we have developed a differential approach to study the electron transfer mediating properties across molecular junctions based on a combination of AFM nanolithography and conductive tip atomic microscopy.

(i) CT-AFM can be used for measuring transport through metal-molecules-metal junctions; (ii) a differential approach can be applied to CT-AFM for the study of metal- molecules-metal junctions; and (iii) this differential approach can be used for the determination of transport coefficients of molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a methodology for the study of molecular transport based on the differential measurement of the transport properties of molecular assemblies.
the development of new strategies for the fabrication and the characterization of molecular devices.
the investigation of charge transport through molecular junctions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the differential approach is an effective way to measure absolute transport coefficients in molecular junctions, but it is also a very powerful tool to investigate the transport mechanisms across molecule-substrate and molecule-molecule interfaces.

CT-AFM is a valuable tool to investigate the charge transport properties of molecular assemblies and that the differential approach presented here provides a way to overcome many of the difficulties that are encountered when studying transport properties by means of this technique.
the differential approach allows to determine the differential resistance of the molecular junction and that the differential conductance is independent of the nature of the tip-molecule contact.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a differential approach to measure absolute transport properties of molecular assemblies.

this differential method is able to measure the electron transfer mediating properties (i.e. the tunneling decay constants) of hydrocarbons with a precision better than 10% as a function of the chain length, which is a very significant achievement in the field.
the differential resistance of a molecule is independent of the nature of the substrate and of the length of the molecule.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CT-AFM is a powerful technique that can be used to investigate the electron transfer mediating properties and the morphology of molecular assemblies with high accuracy.

the transport across a molecular junction is a function of the molecular layer that is being contacted by the tip and that the differential resistance is a more reliable measure of transport properties than absolute resistance.
the method is suitable for the determination of differential conductances of any kind of molecular junctions.
